Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0039", "row_sha256": "ded186bce30fe7cf02f85c086de085932763d3fc99ff5ec6b25e2850ab062b70", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need you to draft a short, friendly email invitation for our seed exchange and please make it sound like a neighbor inviting people rather than an official notice. address it to Celeste, not Jasper. The exchange is Saturday, June 7, from 10 a.m. to noon in the Garden Room at Maple Street Community Center. The point is for people to swap vegetable and flower seeds, so mention both kinds. Ask people to bring packets labeled with the plant name and the year collected if they know it. Also make clear that coming is free and that someone can still attend even if they don't have seeds to trade. I want a subject line too, and keep the actual email brief, around one paragraph, not a long explanation of how seed exchanges work. Mention the room and the time plainly so nobody has to dig for them. Please don't address it to a group or write a generic public announcement; this should read as a direct email to the recipient. No RSVP details were given, so don't add any.", "output": "Draft a brief, friendly, one-paragraph email invitation with a subject line, addressed directly to Celeste, not Jasper. Write in the voice of a neighbor, rather than as an official notice or a generic public announcement.\n\nInvite the recipient to the seed exchange on Saturday, June 7, from 10 a.m. to noon in the Garden Room at Maple Street Community Center. Mention that people can swap vegetable and flower seeds, and ask them to bring packets labeled with the plant name and the year collected, if they know it. Make clear that the event is free and that people may attend even if they have no seeds to trade. State the time and room plainly. Keep the email brief and don't add RSVP details or a long explanation of seed exchanges."}]
